statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON. NQ front-month last traded near 29,565.25, up 0.14%, still inside the Sunday restart band of 29,530.50-29,622.75 that has now contained about seven hours of trade. Stress eases one point to 54 as crude gives back part of its weekend gain, WTI to $91.48 and Brent to $96.28, against a ten-year yield near 4.784%, a 58% market-implied probability of a Federal Reserve hike on 16 September, and an Iranian restricted zone outside the Strait of Hormuz that Tehran has signalled but not yet declared.
recommendation: Conditions map to EA_ON for NQ futures and NAS100 CFD. Conditional risk concentrates in the narrow 15:00-17:00 UTC window covering the European cash close into the Labor Day futures pre-open halt, and secondarily at the 22:00 UTC restart for the Tuesday trade date, rather than across the whole outlook. Every forecast hour maps below the block threshold. Existing-position management and emergency protection are unaffected by this mapping.
headline: Nasdaq-100 futures hold their 92-point Sunday restart range into a seventh hour as crude gives back part of the weekend risk premium
body:
Containment remains the defining observation. NQ front-month last printed 29,565.25, up 40.50 points or 0.14%, inside a restart range of 29,530.50 to 29,622.75. That band is about 92 points or 0.31% wide and has now held for roughly seven hours. Investing.com's delayed feed puts the same contract at 29,584.25 on a slightly different reference close; both readings sit inside the band and neither is near an extreme. E-mini S&P futures traded 7,722.00 within a 14-point range over the same window. Repeated extension after failed retracements, shallow pullbacks and holding near session extremes are the structures that overwhelm a reverse or mean-reversion strategy, and none of the three is present, so Tail stays at the low-band floor.

The one genuine change this hour is in energy. WTI has eased to $91.48 and Brent to $96.28, each roughly 1% below where they traded an hour ago, though both remain marginally higher on the day. Reuters had reported Brent near $96.97 and U.S. crude near $92.24 earlier in the session. A weekend risk premium that gives ground while the underlying headlines are unchanged is a mild relief, and Stress moves down one point to 54 to reflect it.

The geopolitical channel itself is unresolved rather than escalating. Iran's Supreme National Security Council secretary Mohsen Rezaei said a restricted zone outside the Strait of Hormuz would be declared within days, beginning at the line of the U.S. Navy blockade and extending into parts of the Gulf, with vessels entering subject to sanctions designation. Parliament speaker Qalibaf said any future attack on Iranian interests would receive a faster, heavier and more painful response. The zone's boundaries and enforcement mechanism have not been published, and Hormuz transits are running near nine million barrels a day, about two-thirds of pre-conflict levels. This is a severe but progressively priced supply disruption, and under the standing method a chronic and already-absorbed channel supports Stress rather than Tail.

The rate and volatility backdrop offers no amplifier. Ten-year Treasury yields sit near 4.7840%, close to their highest since late 2023, with markets pricing a 58% probability of a Federal Reserve hike at the 16 September meeting and 70% by October after Friday's upbeat payrolls report. The H.15 release shows the two-year at 4.34% and the ten-year at 4.77% as of 4 September. Gold has slipped toward $4,406 an ounce on the same repricing. Friday's VIX close of 14.53 is low in absolute terms and leaves no volatility premium to unwind. Asia remains divided rather than aligned: the Nikkei is up around 2% and the Kospi 3.1% on chip demand, while the Hang Seng is down more than 1% and the Hang Seng Tech index about 1.1% lower. A regional technology complex that rallies in Seoul and falls in Hong Kong within one session is rotating, not trending, and NQ has tracked neither leg.

Today is Labor Day. U.S. cash equity and Treasury markets are closed. CME Globex opened normally on Sunday evening but equity-index futures move to a pre-open state at 17:00 UTC, in which orders may be entered, modified or cancelled but not matched, and reopen at 22:00 UTC for the Tuesday trade date. No settlement price is derived or disseminated for Monday. The narrow danger window therefore stays at 15:00 to 17:00 UTC, covering the European cash close into that hard deadline, because a squeeze into a fixed halt in an already thin book remains the most plausible unrepaired-move mechanism in this outlook. It is a conditional scenario, not an observation.

The week is back-loaded and today is empty. August PPI and initial jobless claims arrive on Thursday 10 September, and August CPI on Friday 11 September, the last inflation reading before the 15-16 September FOMC decision, with the Fed already in its pre-meeting communications blackout. None of those events falls inside this 24-hour outlook, and under the standing method event importance and forecast dispersion of that kind inform Stress and Confidence rather than Tail.

Shared delayed cross-asset context was collected at 01:20 UTC and is now more than four hours old, well past its freshness threshold, so it is treated as stale and this assessment rests entirely on independently verified live sources.

lookbackSummary: Twenty-three of the 24 preceding hourly Claude assessments are available; the 21:00 UTC hour on 6 September has no published assessment and is marked unavailable with null fields. Tail held a flat 5 through the closed-venue Sunday session, mapping to EA_ON and green in every available hour, stepped to 8 at the 22:00 UTC restart to carry reopen-gap risk, then eased to 6 and back to 5 once the restart proved orderly and has stayed at 5 for the last six available hours. Stress opened the window at 54, dipped to a 52 low at 07:00 UTC, drifted up through a 54-58 band as Sunday's geopolitical flow accumulated, peaked at 60 at 20:00 UTC, then eased to 57, 56, 55, 54, 54, 55 and 55 after the reopen. Confidence held a narrow 84-86 band and dominant mode was normal in every available hour.
outlookSummary: The next 24 hours cover the rest of the Asian session, a European session traded against closed US cash equity and Treasury markets on Labor Day, a shortened futures session that moves to pre-open at 17:00 UTC, five closed hours, and the 22:00 UTC restart for the Tuesday trade date. Conditional Tail stays inside the low band in every hour: 5 for the current hour and the next while the restart range holds, 6 across the Asian-to-European handover and the European cash open, 7 through the European morning where the weekend Iran and Hormuz headlines first meet real depth without a US cash backstop, 6 through the holiday-thinned midday, 7 across the notional US open and early afternoon, 8 as the danger window opens at the European cash close and 8 in the final hour before the halt, the closed-venue floor of 5 while futures are shut, then 8 at the Tuesday restart easing through 7 and 6 back to 5. Conditional Stress tracks the same shape between 53 and 57, and Confidence decays from 86 to 70 as the assessment ages away from its evidence cutoff.

Conditional only: if crude reverses this hour's decline and European energy leads, cross-asset alignment would firm; the current evidence shows crude easing instead.

The relevant question for the restart is whether the Hormuz restricted-zone boundaries are published while the venue is shut, since an unpriced concrete announcement is a different reopen condition from an unchanged one. That is a checkpoint, not a forecast of its outcome.
